errors.english: These phenomena are neither with affliction nor without affliction.

errors.english: the object to be negated by the cognition and its object is existing because it is designated as existing, and their reversal is the non-existence of non-perception
errors.why: The cognition and its object, i.e. the thing to be negated, are what is called 'existent', and their absence is the 'non-existence' that non-perception establishes; the English makes the cognition the negator and speaks of non-perception itself being non-existent.

errors.english: The other possessing the reason, such as the dewlap and so forth, is to be explained after reversing the reason of the ox
errors.why: The cited line says the other (non-perception) that has a ground will be explained as the absence of the grounds of 'ox', i.e. dewlap etc.; the dewlap is the ground of 'ox', not an example of 'the other'.

errors.english: by using factors that are not incompatible with the body and the mind of an omniscient one
errors.why: The Mīmāṃsakas negate omniscient and passionless beings by reasons such as having a body and intellect, which are not incompatible with omniscience; body and mind are the reasons, not attributes of the omniscient.

note: The broad line of the anupalabdhi discussion survives, but several sentences are mis-parsed so the argument is hard to follow.

errors.english: the observation that things like a rabbit's horns do not exist serves to prove that the subject, space, likewise does not exist
errors.why: The reason 'unproduced' is seen in non-existents such as the hare's horn, and therefore proves the subject space to be non-existent; it is not 'the observation that hare's horns do not exist'.

note: A sound rendering of the svayam / iṣṭa discussion of the thesis; one example of the dharmisvarūpa fallacy is slightly misconstrued.

errors.english: is intended to produce its own aspect
errors.why: mngon par sems pa is the cognition's (mis)construal: the cognition takes [the object] to be the producer of its own aspect; the cognition is not 'intended to produce' anything, and the following 'what is intended' should likewise be 'what is construed'.

errors.english: existence itself does not appear because it is isolated and separated from other things
errors.why: dben pa dang bral ba means 'lacking isolation from others': existence does not appear because it is not something set apart from other things, the opposite of 'isolated and separated'.
